claims.text: System instruction significantly influences factual accuracy across open-source LLMs.
Temperature settings have a minor effect on LLM hallucination behavior compared to system instruction.
Few-shot prompting achieves a mean F1 score of 0.1889 on the TruthfulQA benchmark.
'Say-I-don’t-know' prompts increase semantic alignment in model responses.
Zero-shot responses exhibit higher semantic consistency under embedding-based similarity analyses.

evidence.description: Two-way ANOVA and Tukey post-hoc analyses revealed system instruction significantly influenced factual accuracy across all tested models.
Two-way ANOVA and Tukey post-hoc analyses showed temperature effects were comparatively minor.
Evaluation on TruthfulQA yielded a mean F1 score of 0.1889 for few-shot prompting.
'Say-I-don't-know' prompts led to reduced precision via conservative refusal bias.
Embedding-based similarity analyses confirmed higher semantic consistency for zero-shot responses.

methodologies.name: Factorial Prompting and Temperature Sensitivity Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluates open-source LLMs across different temperatures and prompting paradigms using exact match, token F1, and semantic/embedding similarity metrics analyzed with ANOVA and Tukey tests.

limitations.text: Large Language Models tend to produce factually incorrect or fabricated information.
'Say-I-don't-know' prompts induce a conservative refusal bias, reducing response precision.
